This experiment compares rational backward Euler with exact-discrete fractional
backward Euler on the **same assembled P1 FEM operator**, using the same
initial data, forcing and time steps as `conv_in_m_isolated.Rmd`.
It computes fresh BRASIL coefficients on **one fixed interval for every order**.
The complete numerical eigensystem determines the spectral interval and the
reference solution; the rational solution uses shifted sparse solves.

## Choose the experiment

Edit these settings and run all chunks or Knit. Coefficients are generated at
the requested exponents without table interpolation. Results and coefficients
stay in memory; knitting creates the HTML report. A first full run takes a few
minutes. Python setup is described in `fun/fixed_int/README.md`.

```{r settings}
h <- 0.02
tau <- 0.005
m_max <- 14L
alpha_vector <- seq(0.5, 1.9, 0.2)
T_final <- 1
kappa <- 4
diffusion <- 1

fixed_x_min <- NULL       # Automatic: min(kappa^2/lambda_max, 1/diagnostic_y_max).
diagnostic_y_max <- 1e3   # Also cover the original scalar interval [1,1000].
coefficient_digits <- 70L
coefficient_tolerance <- 1e-8
coefficient_max_iterations <- 2000L
coefficient_workers <- 2L
python <- Sys.getenv("NAP_BRASIL_PYTHON", unset = "") # Default: .venv-fixed-int/bin/python.
compare_package_tables <- TRUE
scalar_grid_points <- 10001L
```

The physical data are $u_0=10e_5$ and $f(t)=10\sin(\pi t)e_7$ on the
tadpole with edge lengths 1 and 2. The equation is
$u_t+\nu L^{\alpha/2}u=f$, where `diffusion` is $\nu$.
The integer case $\alpha=2$ uses ordinary backward Euler exactly and requires
no fitted coefficients. The fixed-interval orders are independent of the
orders available in the installed rSPDE tables.

## Assemble the problem and choose the interval

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache = FALSE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE)
library(Matrix)
library(ggplot2)
source(here::here("fun", "fixed_int", "experiment.R"), local = TRUE)

stopifnot(length(h)==1L,is.finite(h),h>0,
  length(tau)==1L,is.finite(tau),tau>0,
  length(T_final)==1L,is.finite(T_final),T_final>0,
  length(kappa)==1L,is.finite(kappa),kappa>0,
  length(diffusion)==1L,is.finite(diffusion),diffusion>0,
  length(m_max)==1L,is.finite(m_max),m_max>=2,m_max==floor(m_max),
  length(alpha_vector)>0L,!anyDuplicated(alpha_vector),all(is.finite(alpha_vector)),
  all(alpha_vector>=0.5 & alpha_vector<=2),
  length(scalar_grid_points)==1L,is.finite(scalar_grid_points),
  scalar_grid_points>=3,scalar_grid_points==floor(scalar_grid_points))
N <- round(T_final/tau)
if (!is.finite(N) || N<1 || N>1e6 ||
    abs(T_final/tau-N)>64*.Machine$double.eps*max(1,N))
  stop("Choose T_final/tau to be an integer between 1 and 1e6.")
time_seq <- (0:N)*tau
m_vector <- seq_len(m_max)
fractional_alphas <- alpha_vector[alpha_vector!=2]
data <- fixed_int_tadpole_data(h,kappa)
spectrum <- fixed_int_discrete_spectrum(data$C,data$L)
fitting_interval <- fixed_int_interval(spectrum,kappa,fixed_x_min,diagnostic_y_max)
knitr::kable(data.frame(h_requested=h,h_min=data$h_min,h_max=data$h_max,
  tau=tau,steps=N,dimension=nrow(data$C),
  normalized_eigenvalue_max=fitting_interval$spectral_y_max,
  fixed_x_min=fitting_interval$x_min,fixed_x_max=fitting_interval$x_max),digits=10)
data$mesh_backend
```

For $\mathbf L=\kappa^2\mathbf C+\mathbf G$, compute
$\mathbf LV=\mathbf CV\Lambda$ and $V^\top\mathbf CV=I$.
The normalized eigenvalues are $y_j=\lambda_j/\kappa^2$.
The fitting interval is
\[
J=[\delta,1],\qquad
\delta=\min\!\left(\frac{\kappa^2}{\lambda_{\max,h}},
                         \frac{1}{\mathtt{diagnostic\_y\_max}}\right).
\]
This one interval covers the full reciprocal FEM spectrum and the original
scalar diagnostic. It stays fixed as $m$ varies. An explicit `fixed_x_min`
can extend the interval toward zero; a value that misses the spectrum or
scalar diagnostic is rejected. Changing `h` or `kappa` requires regenerating
the coefficients, which this notebook does on every run.

## Compute the BRASIL coefficients

For each $\beta=\alpha/2$ and $m$, BRASIL computes a degree-$(m,m)$
approximation $B_{m,\beta}(x)\approx x^\beta$ on $J$.
Fitting and conversion to partial fractions use extended precision.
Only the final coefficients passed to the sparse solver are rounded to doubles:
\[
S_{m,\beta}(y)=B_{m,\beta}(1/y)
=d_m+\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{\rho_j}{y-\eta_j}.
\]
The constant $d_m=B_{m,\beta}(0)$ is retained. Every fit must converge,
satisfy signed equioscillation, reconstruct its barycentric representation,
and have distinct negative poles, positive residues and $d_m\ge0$.

```{r coefficients}
coefficient_bank <- fixed_int_generate(
  betas=fractional_alphas/2,orders=m_vector,interval=fitting_interval,
  digits=coefficient_digits,tolerance=coefficient_tolerance,
  max_iterations=coefficient_max_iterations,workers=coefficient_workers,python=python)
coefficient_diagnostics <- coefficient_bank$diagnostics
if (nrow(coefficient_diagnostics)) {
  knitr::kable(aggregate(cbind(deviation,equioscillation_gap,double_conversion_gap)~beta,
    coefficient_diagnostics,max),digits=10)
  coefficient_bank$toolchain
}
```

## The matrix update and isolated error

The rational scheme is the same inverse-power scheme derived in
[BRASIL functionality](brasilfunctionality.html#num_scheme), equation (9).
Writing $a=\tau\nu\kappa^{2\beta}$, its time-step multiplier is
\[
H_m(y)=\frac{S_{m,\beta}(y)}{S_{m,\beta}(y)+a}
=c+\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{w_j}{y-q_j},\qquad
c=\frac{d_m}{d_m+a}.
\]
The source poles/residues $(\eta_j,\rho_j)$ differ from the time-step
poles/residues $(q_j,w_j)$. Real scalar bracketing finds the latter without
forming polynomial products. The checked source signs give $q_j<0$ and $w_j>0$.
At each step, with interval-averaged forcing, the implementation computes
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf b^{k+1}&=\mathbf C\mathbf U_m^k+\tau\mathbf F^{k+1},\\
\mathbf U_m^{k+1}
&=c\mathbf C^{-1}\mathbf b^{k+1}
  +\sum_{j=1}^m w_j(\mathbf L/\kappa^2-q_j\mathbf C)^{-1}\mathbf b^{k+1}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Each sparse Cholesky factorization is reused throughout the time history.
The reference uses the exact discrete multipliers
$1/(1+\tau\nu\lambda_j^\beta)$ on the same mesh and time grid. The error is
\[
E_m=\left[\tau\sum_{k=1}^{N}
  (\mathbf U_h^k-\mathbf U_m^k)^\top\mathbf C
  (\mathbf U_h^k-\mathbf U_m^k)\right]^{1/2}.
\]

```{r compute}
references <- lapply(alpha_vector,function(alpha)
  fixed_int_reference(data$C,spectrum,data$initial,data$spatial_load,
                      time_seq,alpha,diffusion))
control_reference <- fixed_int_reference(data$C,spectrum,data$initial,
  data$spatial_load,time_seq,alpha=2,diffusion=diffusion)
control <- fixed_int_error(data,spectrum,control_reference,m=1L)
rows <- list()
for (reference in references) for (m in m_vector)
  rows[[length(rows)+1L]] <- fixed_int_error(data,spectrum,reference,m,bank=coefficient_bank)
results <- fixed_int_mark_resolution(do.call(rbind,rows),control$error)
errors <- matrix(results$error,nrow=length(m_vector),
  dimnames=list(m=m_vector,alpha=alpha_vector))
knitr::kable(errors,format.args=list(scientific=TRUE,digits=5))
```

## Convergence and numerical resolution

Open circles mark errors below the empirical resolution indicator:
the larger of the sparse/eigenbasis error disagreement and the ordinary
backward Euler control error, multiplied by 100. Slopes use resolved points
only. Dashed lines show the original root-exponential benchmark
$-2\pi\sqrt{\alpha/2}$, anchored at $m=1$; it is a comparison slope, not a
predicted rate for approximation on a fixed interval away from zero.

```{r convergence, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
plot_data <- results
plot_data$alpha_label <- factor(plot_data$alpha,levels=alpha_vector)
guides <- plot_data[plot_data$alpha!=2,]
for (alpha in fractional_alphas) {
  index <- which(guides$alpha==alpha)
  guides$error[index] <- guides$error[index[1L]]*
    exp(-2*pi*sqrt(alpha/2)*(sqrt(guides$m[index])-1))
}
p_m_fixed_int <- ggplot(plot_data,aes(sqrt(m),error,colour=alpha_label,group=alpha_label))+
  geom_line()+geom_point(aes(shape=resolved),size=2)+
  geom_line(data=guides,linetype="dashed")+
  scale_shape_manual(values=c(`FALSE`=1,`TRUE`=16))+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=sqrt(m_vector),labels=m_vector)+
  scale_y_continuous(trans=scales::log_trans(base=exp(1)),labels=scales::label_scientific())+
  labs(x="m (square-root positions)",y="Isolated space-time error (natural-log scale)",
    colour="alpha",shape="Resolved",
    subtitle=sprintf("Fresh BRASIL on [%g, 1]; h=%g; tau=%g",fitting_interval$x_min,h,tau))+
  theme_minimal()+theme(legend.position="bottom")
p_m_fixed_int
slopes <- fixed_int_slopes(results)
knitr::kable(slopes,digits=6)
```

The table also fits $\log E_m$ against $m$, since fixed-interval convergence
can look exponential in $m$. Both fits describe this finite-dimensional
experiment; neither establishes a mesh-uniform asymptotic rate.

## Compare with the installed tables

This optional comparison changes only the coefficients, using the same
assembled matrices, loads, steps, sparse solver and reference. Unsupported or
invalid table entries are reported and omitted. They do not limit the orders
available to the freshly computed coefficients.

```{r table-comparison, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
table_rows <- rejected_rows <- list()
if (compare_package_tables) {
  for (reference in references) for (m in m_vector) {
    cf <- tryCatch(if(reference$alpha==2) NULL else
      fixed_int_table_coefficients(m,reference$alpha/2),error=function(e)e)
    if (inherits(cf,"error")) {
      rejected_rows[[length(rejected_rows)+1L]] <- data.frame(
        alpha=reference$alpha,m=m,reason=conditionMessage(cf))
      next
    }
    table_rows[[length(table_rows)+1L]] <- fixed_int_error(data,spectrum,reference,m,
      coefficients=cf,source="Installed tables")
  }
}
table_results <- if(length(table_rows))
  fixed_int_mark_resolution(do.call(rbind,table_rows),control$error) else NULL
table_rejections <- if(length(rejected_rows)) do.call(rbind,rejected_rows) else NULL
if (!is.null(table_rejections)) knitr::kable(table_rejections)
if (!is.null(table_results)) {
  comparison <- rbind(results,table_results)
  comparison$alpha_label <- factor(comparison$alpha,levels=alpha_vector,
    labels=paste("alpha =",alpha_vector))
  p_table_comparison <- ggplot(comparison,
    aes(sqrt(m),error,colour=source,linetype=source,group=source))+
    geom_line()+geom_point(aes(shape=resolved),size=1.5)+
    facet_wrap(~alpha_label,ncol=4,scales="free_y")+
    scale_shape_manual(values=c(`FALSE`=1,`TRUE`=16))+
    scale_y_log10(labels=scales::label_scientific())+
    labs(x="sqrt(m)",y="Isolated space-time error",colour="Coefficients",linetype="Coefficients",
      shape="Resolved",subtitle="Matched FEM/backward Euler problem; only the coefficients differ")+
    theme_minimal()+theme(legend.position="bottom")
  print(p_table_comparison)
  matched_slopes <- do.call(rbind,lapply(alpha_vector,function(alpha) {
    old <- table_results[table_results$alpha==alpha,]
    fresh <- results[results$alpha==alpha,]
    orders <- intersect(old$m[old$resolved],fresh$m[fresh$resolved])
    slope <- function(d) if(length(orders)>=2L)
      unname(coef(lm(log(error)~sqrt(m),d[d$m%in%orders,]))[2L]) else NA_real_
    data.frame(alpha=alpha,matched_orders=paste(orders,collapse=","),
      table_slope=slope(old),fixed_interval_slope=slope(fresh))
  }))
  knitr::kable(matched_slopes,digits=6)
}
```

## Scalar errors on exactly reciprocal fixed intervals

These diagnostics use the **same freshly computed coefficients** as the matrix
solution and the full common interval $[1,1/\delta]$:
\[
|S_{m,\beta}(y)-y^{-\beta}|
=|B_{m,\beta}(x)-x^\beta|,\qquad x=1/y.
\]
The two errors are evaluated independently on exactly reciprocal grids. Their
sampled maxima agree up to roundoff. These are sampled errors, not certified
uniform bounds. Changing the interval with $m$ would change this experiment.

```{r scalar-errors}
scalar_y <- exp(seq(0,log(fitting_interval$y_max),length.out=scalar_grid_points))
scalar_x <- 1/scalar_y
scalar_rows <- scalar_summary_rows <- list()
for (alpha in fractional_alphas) for (m in m_vector) {
  beta <- alpha/2
  cf <- fixed_int_coefficients(coefficient_bank,m,beta)
  inverse_error <- abs(fixed_int_inverse(scalar_y,cf)-scalar_y^(-beta))
  power_error <- abs(fixed_int_power(scalar_x,cf)-scalar_x^beta)
  gap <- max(abs(inverse_error-power_error))
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(c(inverse_error,power_error))),gap<1e-12)
  scalar_rows[[length(scalar_rows)+1L]] <- data.frame(
    alpha=alpha,m=m,y=scalar_y,x=scalar_x,absolute_error=inverse_error,power_error=power_error)
  scalar_summary_rows[[length(scalar_summary_rows)+1L]] <- data.frame(
    alpha=alpha,m=m,sampled_inverse_max=max(inverse_error),sampled_power_max=max(power_error),
    reciprocal_gap=gap)
}
scalar_errors <- if(length(scalar_rows)) do.call(rbind,scalar_rows) else NULL
scalar_max_errors <- if(length(scalar_summary_rows)) do.call(rbind,scalar_summary_rows) else NULL
if (!is.null(scalar_errors)) {
  scalar_errors$alpha_label <- factor(scalar_errors$alpha,levels=fractional_alphas,
    labels=paste("alpha =",fractional_alphas))
  scalar_errors$m_label <- factor(scalar_errors$m,levels=m_vector)
  scalar_max_errors$alpha_label <- factor(scalar_max_errors$alpha,levels=fractional_alphas)
  knitr::kable(scalar_max_errors,format.args=list(scientific=TRUE,digits=5))
}
```

```{r scalar-error-curves, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
if (!is.null(scalar_errors)) {
  # Exact zero samples at crossings are omitted on the logarithmic error axis.
  positive_errors <- scalar_errors[scalar_errors$absolute_error>0,]
  p_scalar_fixed_int <- ggplot(positive_errors,
    aes(y,absolute_error,colour=m_label,group=m_label))+
    geom_line(linewidth=.5)+facet_wrap(~alpha_label,ncol=4)+scale_x_log10()+
    scale_y_log10(labels=scales::label_scientific())+
    labs(x="Normalized spectral variable y",y="Absolute inverse-power error",colour="m",
      subtitle=sprintf("Fresh BRASIL; common y interval [1, %g]",fitting_interval$y_max))+
    theme_minimal()+theme(legend.position="bottom")
  print(p_scalar_fixed_int)
}
```

```{r unit-interval-error-curves, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
if (!is.null(scalar_errors)) {
  positive_errors <- scalar_errors[scalar_errors$power_error>0,]
  p_power_fixed_int <- ggplot(positive_errors,aes(x,power_error,colour=m_label,group=m_label))+
    geom_line(linewidth=.5)+facet_wrap(~alpha_label,ncol=4)+scale_x_log10()+
    scale_y_log10(labels=scales::label_scientific())+
    labs(x="Reciprocal variable x",y="Absolute power error",colour="m",
      subtitle=sprintf("Same coefficients; common x interval [%g, 1]",fitting_interval$x_min))+
    theme_minimal()+theme(legend.position="bottom")
  print(p_power_fixed_int)
}
```

```{r scalar-error-convergence, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
if (!is.null(scalar_max_errors)) {
  p_scalar_m_fixed_int <- ggplot(scalar_max_errors,
    aes(sqrt(m),sampled_inverse_max,colour=alpha_label,group=alpha_label))+
    geom_line()+geom_point(size=2)+
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=sqrt(m_vector),labels=m_vector)+
    scale_y_continuous(trans=scales::log_trans(base=exp(1)),labels=scales::label_scientific())+
    labs(x="m (square-root positions)",y="Sampled maximum scalar error (natural-log scale)",
      colour="alpha",subtitle="Same fixed interval and coefficients for every order")+
    theme_minimal()+theme(legend.position="bottom")
  print(p_scalar_m_fixed_int)
}
```

## Numerical checks

`product_error` evaluates the same $S_{m,\beta}$ directly in the complete
numerical eigenbasis and evolves every mode. It uses no time-step partial
fractions. Its agreement with the sparse result checks the implementation
of the rational scheme. The exact-integer control checks ordinary backward
Euler against the same discrete reference.

```{r checks}
knitr::kable(spectrum$diagnostics,digits=10)
knitr::kable(control[,c("error","product_error","final_state_gap_C")],
  format.args=list(scientific=TRUE,digits=5))
knitr::kable(results[,c("alpha","m","error","product_error",
  "absolute_error_disagreement","reconstruction_error","resolved")],
  format.args=list(scientific=TRUE,digits=5))
```

This study measures rational error at fixed `h` and `tau`. Faster observed
decay on this finite spectral interval does not imply a faster mesh-uniform
rate for approximation down to zero. Values near the numerical floor are
shown for completeness and excluded from the reported resolved slopes.
